# How to contribute to Stan?

::: {.callout-important}
You [don't]{.hl} need to be a professional software developer or statistician in order to contribute to Stan!
::: 

## Types of contributions
There are many ways to contribute to Stan, including:

- [asking and answering questions]{.hl} of users on [Discourse](https://discourse.mc-stan.org)
- [reporting problems]{.hl} when interacting with the software or documentation
- [requesting new features]{.hl} or improvements
- providing [feedback on documentation]{.hl}
- contributing with a [case study]{.hl} of your specific research field
- contributing [code]{.hl}

---

## Typical workflows for contributing

### Participate in the Stan Discourse

- [Discourse](https://discourse.mc-stan.org) is the main forum for users and
developers to ask questions, discuss issues, and share ideas.
- we want a friendly and welcoming environment
  + [Code of Conduct](https://mc-stan.org/code-of-conduct.html)
  + [Discourse guidelines](https://discourse.mc-stan.org/guidelines)

---

### Feature requests and bug reports

- Go to the GitHub repository ![](img/github_logo.png){width="2%"} of interest
- Get familiar with Issues and PRs ([Example: loo](https://github.com/stan-dev/loo/issues))
- For new contributors: 
  + check for labels like "help wanted" or "good first issue"
  + avoid working on issues that incorporate refactoring or larger changes
  + when in doubt, ask in the issue whether it's a good idea to work on it
- Open a new Issue
  + Check first whether the issue already exists
  + Some tips for writing good Issues...

---

### Feature requests and bug reports

::: {.callout-note}
## Writing good Issues: Bug Report

+ Title: One sentence, specific, searchable.
+ Body
  + What happened vs what you expected
  + Minimal reproducible example (i.e., small model/script/data that triggers the problem)
  + (Optional) Environment: OS, hardware if relevant
  + Exact steps to reproduce the problem.
  + Logs / error output (if possible as text in a code block, not a screenshot, so it's searchable)

+ Examples: 
  + [bayesplot](https://github.com/stan-dev/bayesplot/issues/425)
  + [brms](https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/1899)
:::

---

### Feature requests and bug reports

::: {.callout-note}
## Writing good Issues: Feature Request

+ Title: One sentence, specific, searchable.
+ Body
  + describe the problem or limitation
  + (optional) propose solution
  + (optional) note scope of Issue: small, self-contained or does it open a design discussion?

+ Examples:
  + [bayesplot](https://github.com/stan-dev/bayesplot/issues/73)
:::

---

### Feedback on documentation

- unclear documentation
- contribute with new case study or tutorial in your field
- improve existing documentation
- let us know if something is missing
- typos, etc.

---

### Contributing Code

#### Opening a PR

- some packages have templates others don't

::: {.callout-note}
## Writing good PRs

Before you start:
+ [x] Have you read the contributing guidelines?
+ [x] Have you read the [AI Contribution Policy](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/AI-Contribution-Policy)?
+ [x] Are you aware of the Code of Conduct?
For contributing to Stan core libraries:
+ [x] Have you checked the[Developer Wiki](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki)?

**Title:** One sentence, specific, searchable.
**Body:**
+ [x] Link PR to Issue via [GitHub keywords](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue#linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue-using-a-keyword) like `Fixes #123` or `Closes #123`
+ [x] What has been changed and why?
+ [x] (if applicable) Have you added tests and do they pass?
+ [x] (if applicable) Have you added documentation?
+ [x] (if applicable) In case you provided a new vignette, have rendered it locally?
+ [x] Have you ensured that you follow the style of the existing code/docs?
+ [x] Are there any uncertainties or open questions?
+ [x] For transparency: Disclose if you used an AI assistant and commit that you reviewed the changes critically.

**Examples:** 
+ [bayesplot](https://github.com/stan-dev/bayesplot/issues/425)
+ [brms](https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/1899)
:::

---

### Some reflections on the use of AI-assisted development

+ [Stan AI Contribution Guideline](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/AI-Contribution-Policy)
+ Use your own words when writing the PR description and comments in a PR review process
+ Review all changes made by an AI assistant critically and ask yourself:
  - Is this change correct? Do I need this change? Is this change in the scope of the PR?
+ When in doubt about something, ask rather the Stan developers than the AI assistant

---

## Where to find information 

+ different layers of documentation
+ mental model following the [Diátaxis](https://diataxis.fr/) framework:

::: {.fragment}
| Type | Focus | Stan examples |
| :---- | :----- | :------------ |
| Reference | what | Function/package index, Stan math docs, Stan reference manual |
| How-to guides | solve my problem | Vignettes, case studies |
| Tutorials | learn by doing | User's Guide walkthroughs, example-models |
| Explanation | why it's designed this way | Wiki, discussions on Discourse |
:::

---

#### Short primer: R workflow

```{r}
#| eval: false

library(cmdstanr)
library(bayesplot)
library(loo)
library(brms)

stan_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  vector[N] y;
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  mu ~ normal(0, 10);      // prior
  sigma ~ exponential(1);  // prior
  target += normal_lpdf(y | mu, sigma);  // likelihood
}
"
writeLines(stan_code, "model.stan")
mod <- cmdstanr::cmdstan_model("model.stan")

stan_data <- list(N = 20, y = rnorm(20, mean = 5, sd = 2))
fit <- mod$sample(data = stan_data, chains = 4, iter_sampling = 1000)
draws <- fit$draws(variables = c("mu", "sigma"))

bayesplot::mcmc_trace(draws)
loo::loo(brms::log_lik(fit))
```

---

#### Reference ("What")

+ *"What counts as a valid Stan program? What are blocks, types, and constraints, and how do they behave?"*
  - see [Stan reference manual](https://mc-stan.org/docs/2_39/reference-manual/)
  - grammar/rules of the Stan language
  - analogous to a grammar book
+ *"What does `normal_lpdf` do, and what arguments/types does it expect?"*
  - see [Functions reference](https://mc-stan.org/docs/2_39/functions-reference/)
  - built-in vocabulary of the Stan language
  - analogous to a dictionary
+ *"What does `loo()` in the loo R package do, and what arguments does it take?"*
  - see Package index (API) of corresponding downstream package
  - Examples: [loo](https://mc-stan.org/loo/reference/index.html), [ShinyStan](https://mc-stan.org/shinystan/)
  - Analogous to a manual for a specific translation tool

---

#### How-to guides ("Solve my problem")

+ *"How do I fit a Stan model?"*
  - see [Stan user guide](https://mc-stan.org/docs/2_39/user-guide/index.html)
+ *"How do I plot MCMC draws with bayesplot?"*
  - see [Vignette in bayesplot](https://mc-stan.org/bayesplot/articles/plotting-mcmc-draws.html)
+ *"How do I perform leave-one-out cross validation with loo?"*
  - see [Vignette in loo](https://mc-stan.org/loo/articles/loo2-example.html)
+ *"How do I estimate multivariate models in brms?"*
  - see [Vignette in brms](https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/articles/brms_multivariate.html)
+ Etc.

---

#### Tutorials ("Learn by doing")

+ [Tutorials on Stan](https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/tutorials.html#tutorials)
+ Case Studies:
  - [Stan website](https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/case-studies.html)
  - [Bayesian Workflow book](https://avehtari.github.io/Bayesian-Workflow/casestudies.html)
  - on [Aki Vehtari's website](https://users.aalto.fi/~ave/casestudies.html)
+ Published papers
  - [posterior: Tools for Working with Posterior Distributions in R](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.10526)
  - [brms: An R Package for Bayesian Multilevel Models Using Stan](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v080i01)
  - [Visualization in Bayesian workflow](https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/rssa.12378)
  - etc.

#### Explanation ("Why it's designed this way")

+ *"Why is Stan designed this way?"*
  - see [Discourse discussions](https://discourse.mc-stan.org)
  - see [Wiki](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki)
